title: Review queue split view: mandatory purchase date, stock_epoch past-order banner
goal: A human can open any parsed-but-unreviewed receipt, see the source document next to its extracted lines, resolve every ambiguous line (needs_review/new_item), and confirm a purchase date, so the receipt reaches a state where S-13's commit action is safe to run.
in_scope: New route /review: lists receipts with status='parsed' (awaiting review), newest first, linking to /review/[id]. A link from the Today page (app/page.tsx) surfaces the count when > 0, so the flow is discoverable without a global nav (none exists yet in this repo).

New route /review/[id]: split view. Left pane = document preview via lib/receipts/storage.ts's existing getSignedReceiptUrl (img tag for image mimes, <embed>/<iframe> for application/pdf; text/html and multipart/related (mhtml) get a plain 'open original' link instead of inline rendering — mhtml has no good inline-render story in a browser and isn't worth building for this estimate). Right pane = editable line table.

Migration: receipts.purchased_at_confirmed boolean not null default false (additive). Purchase date field on the page is prefilled from receipts.purchased_at if set, else defaults to today client-side only (not written). A single Server Action confirmPurchaseDateAction(receiptId, dateString) validates dateString is a real date, writes purchased_at=dateString and purchased_at_confirmed=true together (never a path that clears purchased_at while leaving the flag true), and sets date_source: 'manual' when the confirmed value differs from what was already stored, otherwise leaves the existing date_source ('document', from this story's extract.ts patch) untouched. This is the only mutation path for purchased_at — no separate clear/unset action exists, so 'empty date blocks commit' holds by construction (A21).

lib/llm/extract.ts patch (one field, additive): sets receipts.date_source='document' when result.object.purchased_at is non-null, else leaves it null. Currently unset entirely, which silently breaks F7's provenance display ('unconfirmed' badge) — a real gap this story closes since it's a hard prerequisite for the date-confirmation UI to mean anything.

Past-order banner: rendered from the CURRENT confirmed purchased_at on every server render (the review page is a server component re-fetched after every mutating Server Action via revalidatePath, so the banner and its checkbox are never stale relative to an edited date). Shown only when purchased_at_confirmed=true and purchased_at < household.stock_epoch: 'Past order — updates history, not current stock', with a 'still have it on hand' override checkbox. The checkbox's value is client-side, scoped to the current confirmed date, and is passed straight into S-13's commit action call as pastOrderOverride — it is not persisted as its own column (only meaningful at the single moment of commit).

Near-duplicate soft warning: if receipts.near_duplicate_of is set (S-08, computed but never surfaced anywhere yet), show a non-blocking banner naming the other receipt id. Closes the deferred UI note left in S-08's migration comment.

Line table, one row per non-excluded receipt_line: 'excluded' lines are hidden behind a collapsed 'N non-inventory rows excluded' note (already resolved, terminal, never need action). 'matched' lines render read-only (item name, matched catalog item, qty_base, unit_price) — F6's sticky-categorization/unit invariant means their category/base_unit are never editable here. 'needs_review' and 'new_item' lines render editable fields (item_name, brand, category dropdown sourced from the live seeded leaf categories, qty_display, unit_display) plus three per-line actions: 'Save & match' (re-runs the S-09/S-10 ladder once, synchronously, against the edited text/category — a human-triggered, single-line operation, never invoked automatically and never part of the commit path), 'Confirm as new item' (locks review_state='new_item' with the edited fields; rejected server-side if category_slug is still 'uncategorized'), 'Mark non-inventory' (sets review_state='excluded', is_non_inventory=true — covers the case where extraction missed a fee/discount row).
canonicalize.ts: export matchCatalogItem (currently module-private) so the 'Save & match' Server Action can reuse S-09's exact matching logic instead of re-implementing it.

Commit button (calls S-13's Server Action): disabled client-side, AND rejected server-side by S-13's own guard, unless purchased_at_confirmed=true and zero receipt_lines for this receipt remain review_state='needs_review'.
out_of_scope: The commit write path itself (creating catalog_items/item_aliases for new_item lines, stock_movements, price_history, item_stats) — that is S-13, this story only gets a receipt into a committable state.

Cancelled/refunded detection banner — working spec F7 mentions it, but no REQ or acceptance criterion in the PRD/backlog tests it; not built here, flagged as a gap for whoever picks it up later (no story currently owns it).

A persisted top-3 candidate picker or a new multi-row matching RPC — find_best_alias_match is deliberately limit-1 (S-09); re-editing a line's text/category and re-running the existing ladder via 'Save & match' is the mechanism instead of building a second RPC and picker UI to serve a want-to-have from F4's prose that no acceptance criterion requires.
Manual entry (E-11) and the merge tool (E-11/S-30) — separate epics.
Editing merchant/total_amount/receipt-level fields other than purchase date — no acceptance criterion needs it.
acceptance: A document with no extractable date blocks commit; setting a date manually releases it (A21).
invariants: purchased_at and purchased_at_confirmed are always written together by a single action — there is no code path that leaves purchased_at set but purchased_at_confirmed false after a prior confirm, nor one that clears purchased_at while the flag stays true.
The past-order override checkbox reflects the currently confirmed date on every render, not a value captured at first page load.
A line's category/base_unit is only ever editable while review_state is 'needs_review' or 'new_item' — never for 'matched' (F6 sticky rule, S-09 invariant carried forward unchanged).
'Save & match' operates on exactly one receipt_line and never writes to any other row — it is not part of, and must never be folded into, S-13's atomic commit function.
